items.longBusinessSummary: Oracle Corporation offers products and services that build, run and support enterprise information technology frameworks worldwide. Its Oracle cloud software as a service offering includes various cloud software applications, including Oracle Fusion cloud enterprise resource planning ERP, Oracle Fusion cloud enterprise performance management EPM, Oracle Fusion cloud supply chain and manufacturing management SCM, Oracle Fusion cloud human capital management HCM, and NetSuite applications suite, Oracle Health applications, as well as Oracle Fusion Sales, Service, and Marketing. The company also offers cloud-based industry solutions for various industries; Oracle cloud license and on-premise license; and Oracle license support services. In addition, it provides cloud and license business' infrastructure technologies, such as the Oracle Database and MySQL Database; Java, a software development language; and middleware, including development tools and others. The company's cloud and license business' infrastructure technologies also comprise cloud-based compute, storage, and networking capabilities; and Oracle autonomous database, as well as AI, Internet-of-Things, machine learning, digital assistant, and blockchain. Further, it provides hardware products and other hardware-related software offerings, including Oracle engineered systems, enterprise servers, storage solutions, industry-specific hardware, virtualization software, operating systems, management software, and related hardware support services, and consulting and advanced customer services. It markets and sells its cloud, license, hardware, support, and services offerings directly to businesses in various industries, government agencies, and educational institutions, as well as through indirect channels. Oracle Corporation has a strategic alliance with Metron, Inc. The company was founded in 1977 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

Title: Alliance Announces Official Oracle NetSuite Partnership & Appoints Stephen Rafferty as Director in the NetSuite Practice
Author: PR Newswire   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 1:00 PM GMT+1 4 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T12:00:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
Strategic partnership and new leadership appointment reinforce Alliance's continued investment in ERP transformation, technology solutions, and financial operations.
TYSONS CORNER, Va., Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Alliance, a national consulting firm specializing in solutions for the Office of the CFO, is proud to announce its official partnership with Oracle NetSuite, a leading cloud-based enterprise resource planning (ERP) platform. The announcement marks a significant milestone in Alliance's continued expansion of its Business Systems & Transformation capabilities and its commitment to helping organizations modernize financial operations, improve efficiency, and support sustainable growth.
Alliance launched its dedicated NetSuite practice earlier this year in response to growing demand for integrated, scalable technology solutions that connect finance, accounting, and business operations. Building on the firm's established expertise in financial advisory, accounting advisory, and business transformation, the practice helps organizations navigate complex ERP initiatives with a combination of technical expertise and deep financial and operational insight.
As an official NetSuite partner, Alliance is further strengthening its ability to help clients evaluate, implement, optimize, and maximize the value of their ERP investments. The partnership supports Alliance's broader commitment to delivering technology-enabled solutions that improve financial visibility, streamline business processes, and equip leadership teams with the insights needed to make informed decisions.
"Becoming an official NetSuite partner is an exciting milestone for Alliance and a natural extension of the work we already do to help finance organizations operate more effectively," said Ed Barrow, CEO of Alliance. "We launched our NetSuite practice with a clear vision: to combine deep financial and accounting expertise with leading technology solutions. This partnership, along with our continued investment in exceptional talent, positions us to deliver even greater value to our clients."
As part of its continued investment in the practice, Alliance is also pleased to announce that Stephen Rafferty has joined the firm as Director of Business Development for the NetSuite Practice.
In this role, Rafferty will focus on driving new business for Alliance's NetSuite practice, building pipeline, deepening partner relationships across the NetSuite ecosystem, and expanding the firm's client base for ERP implementation, optimization, and transformation engagements.
His appointment reflects Alliance's strategic focus on building a team of experienced professionals who understand both the NetSuite market and the business challenges organizations face as they grow and evolve.
"Stephen's arrival is another step in building a NetSuite practice that delivers real results for our clients," said Nikki Tercero, Partner of Business Systems and Transformation at Alliance. "We're committed to investing in leaders who bring the experience, perspective, and client-first approach that define Alliance. With Stephen helping grow this practice, we're excited about what's ahead."
Helping Organizations Connect Technology with Business Performance
Alliance's NetSuite practice is designed to support organizations at various stages of their ERP journey, from evaluating technology needs and preparing for implementation to optimizing existing environments and improving financial processes.
By combining NetSuite capabilities with Alliance's broader consulting expertise, the firm helps organizations address critical business priorities, including:
ERP Strategy & Implementation: Aligning technology investments with business objectives and supporting successful system deployments.
NetSuite Optimization: Improving system functionality, workflows, and processes to maximize the value of existing investments.
Financial Process Transformation: Streamlining accounting and finance operations to improve efficiency, consistency, and scalability.
Reporting & Analytics: Enhancing financial visibility and access to actionable business insights.
Ongoing Advisory & Support: Providing experienced resources and strategic guidance as business and technology needs evolve.
With more than 100 full-time consultants and a growing national presence, Alliance continues to expand its ability to support organizations facing increasingly complex financial, operational, and technology challenges.
The NetSuite partnership and appointment of Rafferty underscore the firm's long-term commitment to building integrated consulting capabilities that help clients move beyond system implementation to achieve meaningful business outcomes.
To learn more about Alliance's NetSuite capabilities.
Alliance is a national consulting firm dedicated to providing the people, expertise, and solutions organizations need to navigate complex business challenges. Specializing in solutions for the Office of the CFO, Alliance offers Accounting Advisory, Finance Advisory, Mergers & Acquisitions, Business Systems & Transformation, AI & Analytics, and Human Capital Solutions. With a team of more than 100 experienced consultants nationwide, including many former Big Four professionals, Alliance partners with organizations across industries to deliver practical solutions and lasting results. The People You Need, The Partner You Want.

Title: What Mattered Most In IBM's Latest Quarter?
Author: Trefis Team   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 12:22 PM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T11:22:20+00:00
=== BODY ===
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
Shares of International Business Machines (IBM) rose 0.26% on October 22, 2026, during the session following its fiscal Q3 2026 report, while the S&P 500 fell 1.2%. Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle each fell more than 2% that day. Revenue came in just 0.7% above analysts' estimates and earnings per share topped expectations by 2.2%. With a beat this small, the more telling changes sit further down the report.So where did IBM's quarter actually turn?
The turn came in software, which generated 44.4% of IBM's revenue in fiscal 2025, more than any other segment. Management said software revenue growth jumped four points from the second quarter to reach 9%. It also said the division led a broader pickup across IBM's segments, with infrastructure growth rising to 5%.
Management said the biggest difference came from a single part of the software business. On the October 21 call, executives explained that transactional sales, the software IBM sells in individual deals rather than as recurring revenue, make up about 20% of the software book. These sales fell by double digits in the second quarter, taking 4 to 5 points off software growth. In the third quarter, they rose by double digits. This swing was larger than software's four-point pickup. Management also said its automation business faced a tougher comparison.
How Much Of IBM's Software Jump Was Catch-Up?
Management said about a quarter of the jump came from large deals that slipped out of the second quarter and closed in the third. The other three-quarters was new business. For transaction processing, its mainframe software, management said the deferred second-quarter deals landed on top of a normal third-quarter mainframe buying cycle.
For IBM as a whole, the quarter looks more like a recovery from the second quarter than a step up. Total reported revenue grew 4.7% from a year earlier, an improvement from 1.1% in the second quarter. That pace still trails the first quarter, when revenue grew 9.5%.
Management held its forecast for 2026 revenue growth at 4% to 5% at constant currency, the same range it gave in July. The company also raised its forecast for the year's increase in free cash flow to more than $1 billion. For the software division, management now expects full-year growth of about 7% to 8%.
Management also expects part of the quarter's strength to fade. Transaction processing, IBM's mainframe software, grew 10% in the quarter. Executives do not expect that double-digit pace to continue, noting that growth might moderate from the third quarter into the fourth. While Red Hat bookings grew in the high teens, and management said such bookings growth turns into good revenue growth, the company did not want to comment on 2027 growth. It said it would quantify its view in January.
IBM's full-year 2026 software growth, measured against management's forecast of about 7% to 8%, is the figure to watch when the company reports in January 2027.

Title: Can Adobe Stock Jump 50%?
Author: Trefis Team   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 12:15 PM GMT+1 4 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T11:15:15+00:00
=== BODY ===
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
To gauge whether Adobe (ADBE) stock can jump 50%, look at a part of the company you may overlook: its faster-growing subscriptions for business professionals and consumers. In seven of the last ten calendar years, the stock rose 50% or more from one close to a later close in the same year. Yet the shares lost 27.0% over the past year, and you probably still think of Adobe as software for creative professionals. So how big are those subscriptions?
Business Professionals And Consumers Bring Adobe 29% Of Subscriptions
Adobe sold $1.91 billion of subscriptions to business professionals and consumers in fiscal Q3 2026, up 16% from a year earlier. That pace makes them the faster-growing group so far. Adobe's subscriptions for creative and marketing professionals were far larger at $4.65 billion, but grew 13%.
Adobe maintains a wide reach with business professionals and consumers. On the September 10, 2026 call, management said monthly active users in this group rose more than 25% from a year earlier to over 900 million. The company is also targeting the next generation of business professionals by making student spaces in Acrobat available globally.
Analysts questioned that approach on the call. When one analyst noted that net new annual recurring revenue was down 36% to 37% from a year earlier, management cited the shift toward freemium products as one of the drivers. Adobe finished fiscal Q3 2026 with $22.16 billion in remaining performance obligations, which represent contracted revenue the company has yet to book. That figure was up 8% from a year earlier.
Trading at 14.0 times Adobe's last twelve months of earnings, against 22.9 for the S&P 500, the stock price appears to allow for little from those users. Adobe's faster-growing business and consumer subscriptions show reported sales are still rising, but they do not settle the analysts' questions about new recurring revenue. Management raised its fiscal 2026 revenue and earnings targets on the call, but it only reiterated its target of 10.2% growth in ending annual recurring revenue.
Adobe opted not to focus on pricing actions in its creative business so it could keep adding users. Management said on the September 10 call that the company was glad it had held back. Pricing actions might have brought short-term relief, management said, but they mattered less than winning new users.
Adobe's sales to business professionals and consumers are growing faster than its sales to creative and marketing professionals so far, while the question of whether its new users will pay remains open. When Adobe reports in December 2026, ending annual recurring revenue compared against management's fiscal 2026 target will be the number to watch.
Is Too Much Of Your Wealth Riding On One Stock?
A stock like Adobe can look very different depending on which part of the business you watch. When one position grows into a large part of your wealth, a sharp fall can hurt your whole plan, and selling to spread the money out can bring a large tax bill.
